or_8_anglin_s_buttress.blurb: Anglin's Buttress is a tall southwest-facing wall of roughly 350 feet in the Monument Area of Smith Rock, Oregon. Most of the ten lines here are bolted, including several long multi-pitch sport routes that climb to the top, along with one crack on gear. Grades run from 5.10 into 5.13, with the bulk sitting in the 5.11 range, so it suits strong leaders rather than newcomers. The rock is the weak point: every line crosses a band of loose, rotten stone low down, and the wall has been described as the poorest rock at Smith. Wear a helmet and expect to pull on suspect holds.

ri_hemlock_ledges.blurb: Hemlock Ledges is a quarter-mile string of small cliffs just south of Beach Pond in Rhode Island, close to the Connecticut line. The tallest part reaches about 45 feet, while much of the rest is lower. Of the ten routes, nearly all are bolted sport lines with one on gear, and most are easy to moderate, from 5.6 to 5.8, with a single 5.10 for a harder pull. Trees on top make top-roping straightforward. It stays shaded for much of the day and can be slow to dry,. A friendly spot for new leaders and anyone building mileage.

ri_black_hut_boulder.blurb: Black Hut Boulder is a single large erratic standing alone among old quarries, within Burrillville, Rhode Island's Black Hut wildlife management area. It rises about 18 feet, and the stone is good quality with honest climbing all the way to the top. Ten problems cover a wide range, from a moderate V2 warm-up through the middle grades to one very hard line near V9. Because it is one boulder rather than a field, plan to pair it with other stops.

ri_fred_boulder.blurb: Fred Boulder is one of the quieter blocks in Lincoln Woods, the main bouldering hub of Rhode Island. It sits beside the road a short way before the Heart Boulder and cannot be seen from the pavement, so it sees fewer visitors than the park's famous stones. Ten problems are on offer, mostly in the V2 to V7 range, with a single very hard line around V10 for the strong. A good add-on stop when you are already working the Heart area, with trails linking it to its neighbors.

ri_buttcrack_wall_and_overhang.blurb: Buttcrack Wall and Overhang is a small bouldering zone in the Railroad Area of Rocky Point, Rhode Island, near the entrance end of the park. The wall is about 12 feet tall and 20 yards long and finishes in a blocky overhang with an arete on each side. The ten problems are unusually varied for such a compact spot: a few easy lines up to V2, a run of middle grades, and several hard problems that reach into the V8 to V12 range. Short and steep, it rewards climbers who like power and tension.
